subject: Discovery recap & procurement framing - ACME Enterprise
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 17:15:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap & procurement framing - ACME Enterprise

Hi Amanda / Raj -

Thanks again for a productive conversation today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum with procurement and the technical teams.

Attendees: Amanda Lee (ACME, Procurement), Raj Patel (ACME, CTO), Marissa Cole (Redwood, AE), Priyom Das (Redwood, SE)

Key pain points discussed:
- High per-token cost and inconsistent latencies on current hosted LLM endpoints (spiky peaks impacting user-facing features).
- Difficulty operationalizing model variants across regions and teams (deployment drift).
- Need for stronger observability and cost breakdown at the token/route level to attribute usage to products.

Current stack:
- ACME uses managed endpoints with VendorX for chat generation and embeddings; Postgres + Redis for session state; runs in us-east-1.
- No dedicated inference fleet today; procurement prefers Opex/usage model but will consider reserved capacity for predictable pricing.

Success criteria (what "good" looks like):
1) 30-50% reduction in per-token inference cost at 99th perc throughput compared to current baseline.
2) End-to-end p95 latency under 350ms for common prompt patterns.
3) Observability and per-route billing to attribute cost by product team.

Procurement framing / decision process (as we discussed):
- Timeline: target decision window is mid-March (~6 weeks) to align with Q2 roadmap.
- Stakeholders: Amanda (Procurement lead), Raj (Technical sponsor), Legal (standard SOW + security review), Platform team (integration owners).
- Initial commercial guardrails: ACME is focused on a predictable unit economics model; initial guardrail discussed on call was a target blended unit price range and a preference for a 12-month committed term if there is a clear cost advantage and SLA.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I will share a short mutual action plan (MAP) outlining milestones, owners, and a proposed commercial guardrail (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Priyom and Raj to validate latency profile and integration points (KV cache, session routing). Can we target next week?
3) Amanda / Procurement to share procurement timeline and any standard PO/SOW requirements so we can surface those in the MAP.

Attachments: 20260210-Redwood-MAP-ACME.pdf (mutual action plan draft)

If that matches your notes, I can loop in Legal/Contracts and send an updated MAP with suggested commercial guardrails we discussed.

Thanks,

-
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - this looks right to me.

A couple clarifications:
- Procurement timeline: legal + procurement review usually takes 3-4 weeks once we have a commercial term sheet.
- Budget guardrail: I can tentatively flag that we have a $X-$Yk/month preferred range for the initial pilot; I need to confirm exact numbers with finance and will share by end of next week.

Happy to get the MAP and set up the technical deep-dive - Raj, do mornings next week work for you?

Amanda
Amanda Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, ACME Enterprise
amanda.lee@acme.com

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & procurement framing - ACME Enterprise

Marissa - thanks for the summary. Two quick technical items to flag before the deep-dive:
1) Security/compliance: we'll need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short summary of data handling for session and KV cache data. Can you attach the SOC2 summary and a brief note on data residency?
2) Latency profile: our traffic is multi-region (primarily us-east + us-west). We'll want to validate p95 across both regions and the behavior under cold cache.

Regards,
Raj
CTO, ACME Enterprise

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & procurement framing - ACME Enterprise

Perfect - thanks Amanda and Raj.

I attached the MAP and a SOC2 summary for your review. Highlights in the SOC2 doc include our audit period, scope (inference control plane), and third-party attestations. Priyom will run the technical deep-dive and validate p95 across both regions; can we propose Tuesday or Wednesday next week (10:00-12:00 PT windows)?

As for procurement, we'll draft an initial commercial guardrail in the MAP (monthly committed and usage overlay options) and flag a 30-day trial period if you want to validate latency/cost before committing.

Next actions:
- Amanda: confirm budget guardrail and procurement contacts (by EOD 2/17)
- Raj: confirm availability for technical deep-dive (Tue/Wed mornings PT)
- Priyom (SE): prepping a short test plan for cold-cache and multi-region p95 tests

Attachments: 20260210-Redwood-MAP-ACME.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.
